title: Introduce 'pocket-econ' autoscaler and compact-batcher with safe quant fallback
author: Nora Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware compact batching autoscaler (pocket-econ) with safe quantization fallback profiles; default presets are non-breaking and behind a feature flag.
body:
Motivation: We see a class of small-to-medium tenants that oscillate between single-token spikes and short bursts. Existing tenant-level autoscalers skew heavy to throughput targets and end up overprovisioning GPU slots or forcing conservative batching that degrades unit economics. This change introduces a lightweight 'pocket-econ' autoscaler that targets per-tenant micro-bursts with compact batching defaults and a controlled quantization fallback path to reduce token cost during transient peaks without impacting tail latency SLAs.

Design summary: pocket-econ is a runtime-side controller that: (1) observes short-window sequence-length and inter-arrival distributions, (2) proposes compact-batcher templates (microbatch shapes tuned for single/short sequences), (3) toggles tenant-local KV prefill strategies for fast warmstarts, and (4) when safe, applies a graded quantization fallback (q8 -> q4 progressive) gated by quality checks and rollback timers. The system is conservative by default: presets are disabled except for tenants opted-in or evaluated via the /admin/econ-sim dry-run API.

What this PR changes: added controller implementation (src/econ/pocket_autoscaler.go), compact batcher templates and presets (configs/presets/pocket-defaults.yaml), a simulation harness and a dry-run CLI for tenant evaluation (tools/simulate_pocket_prefill.py), telemetry hooks and new metrics (src/telemetry/econ_metrics.go), and docs/ops/pocket-econ.md describing behavior and runbooks. Unit and integration tests exercise the rollout and safe-rollback semantics.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of controller and compact batch templates - [x] Simulation harness and dry-run mode - [x] Telemetry and alerts for quality regressions - [x] Feature-flag gating for rollout - [x] Docs and runbook entries - [x] Load tests against the canary pool

Backward compatibility and rollout: By default pocket-econ is feature-flagged off for all tenants. The rollout plan is: 1) enable in staging and run the simulator against production traces (dry-run) 2) enable for a small set of budget-conscious tenants behind a canary flag 3) monitor econ.unit_cost and quality.* metrics for 48 hours 4) progressively widen the cohort. If quant fallback triggers a quality regression, the controller immediately reverts to the last safe quant profile and records a quality-alert event in telemetry.

Testing: Added unit tests for compact batch selection, simulated tenant traces and an integration test that spins up a minimal serving runtime and validates latency SLOs while applying the compact-batcher and quant fallback. CI includes a simulated workload run (tools/simulate_pocket_prefill.py --seed=42 --tenants=50) that completes in ~10 minutes on CI nodes.

Risks and mitigations: The primary risk is quality regressions from quant fallback. Mitigations include staged rollouts, automatic rollback timers, and an offline Monte Carlo evaluator (tools/quant_quality_probe.py referenced in docs) that runs nightly on stored eval prompts. The controller is limited to tenant-specified max_quant_tier and global opt-out.

Related: ENG-1458 (compact batcher templates), ENG-2102 (quant fallback safety harness).

review_comments: Samir Patel: LGTM overall. A few questions on telemetry cardinality — storing tenant_id tags on the heatmap metrics could increase cardinality. Can we emit a sampled tenant tag or aggregate by tenant cohort instead?
Nora Chen: Good catch. Updated econ_metrics.go to emit tenant_cohort and a sampled_tenant tag (1%) for high-cardinality debugging. See commit d4f6c13.

Lena Cho: In integration tests I saw a nondeterministic 99.9th p99.9 spike when quant fallback flipped under load. Can we add a short (150ms) safety-delay before quant changes to avoid mid-inflight degradation?
Nora Chen: Added a gated safety_delay_ms config and adjusted the controller to apply quant changes only between batch windows; updated tests to account for the delay.

Diego Alvarez: CI failed once on the simulate prefills job due to a timeout on the CI runner. After splitting the workload into shards the job passed. Recommend we keep the sharding approach for CI to keep runtime reasonable.
Nora Chen: Sharded the CI simulation and added --ci-shards option to the script; also documented recommended timeout values in docs/ops/pocket-econ.md.
notes: Feature gated; ops teams should read docs/ops/pocket-econ.md before enabling. A follow-up will add a CLI 'pocket-econ audit' that summarizes decisions per tenant.
post_merge_actions: Create canary cohort via admin API (deployed by infra)
Add nightly quant quality probe to eval pipeline
